thread:
maya: Heads-up — did a perf sweep on KV cache behavior after last driver roll. Observed a ~3.8x increase in cache miss rate for some Llama variants when the driver hash changed. Root cause looks like our keying doesn't include driver build id consistently.

maya: Quick snapshot metrics: kv_miss_rate went from 0.04 -> 0.15 for /model/llama/13b:v2 on canary hosts, kv_size_bytes stable, p99_latency_tokens +12ms.

derek: ugh. So we evict on driver changes effectively? What key pieces are we currently using?

maya: Current key = "model_id:prefix_hash:prompt_fingerprint". No driver or runtime id. We tried to be conservative to maximize reuse but that means different binary layouts with incompatible kernels share keys and hit correctness fallbacks or perf cliffs.

rachel: that explains the performance cliffs. We should include a cheap driver/runtime identity but avoid explosion of keys for small driver tweaks. Maybe use driver_hash truncated (8 hex) + seqlen bucket.

jamal: truncating sounds ok, but watch cardinality. If driver teams push nightly hashes we could still bloat. Suggest two levels: persistent per-model keying, plus ephemeral lease for recent driver builds. Lease TTL can let old driver-key combos expire fast.

maya: sketch of proposed key format:```python
# composed key for KV cache
cache_key = f"{model_id}:{model_version}:{driver_hash[:8]}:{seqlen_bucket}:{prefix_hash}"```
seqlen_bucket = floor(min(seq_len, max_len)/bucket_size)  # keeps keys bounded for variable seqs

olga: How do we handle invalidation when we deploy a runtime fix that changes KV layout? We need deterministic invalidation, not manual eviction.

maya: plan: expose invalidation hook from driver deploy pipeline that increments a runtime_epoch per host pool. Invalidation token = driver_hash[:8] if full incompatible change, otherwise bump runtime_epoch field. Runtime reads token at startup and we treat token mismatch as soft-invalidate for affected model namespaces.

jamal: can we implement soft-invalidate as: mark keys stale and let them expire naturally, but also pre-warm hot prefixes by replaying recent requests to new driver? Avoid mass eviction.

rachel: +1. Also add immediate metric kv_invalidation_count and broken_reuse_rate. We should graph by model_version and driver_hash.

derek: any perf regressions from adding driver_hash to key? More keys -> less reuse -> cost up. But safer. Let's quantify: run A/B with 5% traffic where we add driver_hash to key and measure kv_miss_rate and cpu_token_cost.

olga: rollout steps proposal: feature flag (per-pool), canary 5% for 24h, monitor kv_miss_rate, kv_size_bytes, p99_latency_tokens, then 25%/50%/100%. Add automated rollback if p50_latency_tokens increases >10ms or kv_miss_rate >0.2.

maya: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1234 (WIP) — implements key change + invalidation hook + metrics. Needs perf tests.

infra-bot: perf-check started for pr/1234 on canary pool (job id: perf-2387). Results ETA ~2h.

jamal: for persistence we store keys in per-device local shard + optional persistent index in Rocks snapshot. If driver change is compatible, we keep rocks snapshot, otherwise snapshot versioning triggers fallback to rebuild. Need to be careful with snapshot schema changes.

rachel: also add sequence-length-aware eviction priority: small seqlen prefixes have higher reuse; evict large-seqlen keys first under pressure. That should limit byte growth.

derek: agree. Can we add a cheap admission filter: only store keys if token_cost_so_far > threshold? avoids storing tiny prefixes.

maya: yes — threshold default 64 tokens. Will add to PR.

olga: sounds actionable. Next steps: maya finalizes PR, jamal and rachel pair on perf harness + eviction policy, derek will own rollout gating/alerts. I'll draft runbook for invalidation incidents.

maya: thanks. I'll post perf numbers when infra-bot finishes. :coffee:

infra-bot: perf-check completed for pr/1234 on canary pool. Summary: kv_miss_rate (canary) +0.06 absolute, p99_latency_tokens +9ms, kv_size_bytes +3%. Job details: https://ci.redwood/test/perf-2387

derek: that's within our canary gate but borderline. Let's proceed to 25% but keep short window and watch cpu_token_cost.

maya: pushing flag to 25% now. will update thread with metrics in 2h.

jamal: logging note — make sure driver deploy pipeline tags runtime_epoch and exposes driver_compatibility metadata so invalidation can be selective by model.

rachel: tiny UX ask: surface driver_hash and runtime_epoch in per-model dashboard so engineers can correlate regressions quickly.

maya: noted. Thanks all.
